integers.title: What are Integers?
integers.intro: Integers are whole numbers that can be positive, negative, or zero.

absoluteValue.title: Absolute Value
absoluteValue.intro: The absolute value of a number is its distance from zero on the number line.
absoluteValue.explanation: Absolute value is always positive or zero, never negative.

rational.title: Rational Numbers
rational.intro: A rational number is any number that can be written as a fraction p/q, where p and q are integers and q ≠ 0.

numberLine.title: The Number Line
numberLine.explanation: The number line is a visual way to represent integers. Zero is in the middle, positive numbers are to the right, and negative numbers are to the left.

comparing.title: Comparing Integers
comparing.explanation: On a number line, numbers increase as you move to the right and decrease as you move to the left.

addition.title: Adding Integers
addition.rule1: Add the numbers and keep the sign. Example: (-3) + (-5) = -8
addition.rule2: Subtract the smaller absolute value from the larger, and use the sign of the number with larger absolute value. Example: (-7) + 3 = -4

numberLine.title: Integer Number Line
numberLine.caption: Integers extend infinitely in both directions from zero.

absoluteValue.title: Understanding Absolute Value
absoluteValue.caption: Both -4 and 4 are the same distance (4 units) from zero.

comparing.title: Comparing Integer Examples
comparing.caption: On the number line, numbers to the right are always greater.

multiplication.title: Sign Rules for Multiplication
multiplication.caption: The sign of the product depends on the signs of the factors.

numberLine.title: Key Points:
numberLine.point1: Numbers to the right are greater than numbers to the left
numberLine.point2: Negative numbers are less than zero and positive numbers
numberLine.point3: The distance between consecutive integers is always 1

comparing.title: Rules for Comparing:
comparing.rule1: Any positive number is greater than any negative number
comparing.rule2: Between two negative numbers, the one closer to zero is greater (Example: -2 > -5)
comparing.rule3: Zero is greater than all negative numbers and less than all positive numbers

rational.title: Key Facts:
rational.point1: All integers are rational numbers (can be written as n/1)
rational.point2: All terminating decimals are rational numbers
rational.point3: Fractions with non-zero denominators are rational numbers

example1.title: Adding Integers with Different Signs
example1.question: Calculate: (-8) + 12
example1.step3: Subtract: 12 − 8 = 4. Use sign of larger absolute value (positive)

example2.title: Finding Absolute Value
example2.question: What is |-15|?
example2.step1: Absolute value is the distance from zero
example2.step2: The distance from -15 to 0 is 15 units

exercise1.question: Which number is the smallest? -10, -3, 0, 5
exercise1.explanation: -10 is farthest to the left on the number line, so it's the smallest.

exercise2.question: What is |-5|?
exercise2.explanation: The distance from -5 to 0 is 5 units, so |-5| = 5.

exercise3.question: Calculate: (-7) + 5
exercise3.hint: Different signs: subtract and use the sign of the larger absolute value.

notes.title: Tips & Tricks
notes.tip1: 🧮 Remember: The product of two numbers with the same sign is always positive.
notes.tip2: 📍 On a number line, think of negative numbers as being 'below zero' or 'in debt'.
notes.tip3: 💡 When adding integers with different signs, think of it as a 'tug of war' - the stronger side wins!
notes.warning1: ⚠️ Don't confuse the negative sign with subtraction. -5 is a number, while 3 - 5 is an operation.

conclusion.title: Excellent Work! 🎉
conclusion.summary: You've mastered integers and rational numbers! Understanding these concepts is fundamental to all of algebra. You can now work with positive and negative numbers confidently!
conclusion.takeaway1: Integers include positive numbers, negative numbers, and zero
conclusion.takeaway2: Absolute value measures distance from zero and is always non-negative
conclusion.takeaway3: Sign rules for multiplication: same signs = positive, different signs = negative
conclusion.takeaway4: Rational numbers can be expressed as fractions and include all integers and terminating decimals
